Resolves #19174
Refs #19178

The film's splitter resize is a real pointer drag with its live preview. A `resize` cue routes to `GestureDriver#executeResizeStep`, which finds the named split boundary, converts the requested proportion into a pixel travel along the split axis, and hands one atomic drag to `InteractionService#driveDrag` — the product's own drive, the one the Neural Link's `drive_drag` uses — so the Mouse sensor arms the gesture itself and returns a typed receipt. While the drive runs, an escort walks the film cursor on the drive's clock and proves the preview as an observed condition, not a clock sample: a pane box that moved while the committed document stood on both sides of the read and no terminal had landed, sampled through the cursor walk and then polled until the drive settles (`previewTracked`, `documentUnchangedDuringPreview`, `samples`). After the release the executor reads the committed vector from the splitter's own terminal — the reducer's document IS the commit — and waits for the workspace to adopt it by value (`committedOnce`, `sizesAfter`, `synced`), within a tolerance. `applied` is true only with that preview sample, exactly one accepted terminal and the requested vector; each missing proof fails by name. `settleResizeDrive` awaits the physical drive on every failed exit — a destroyed driver included — and reports the live document; the driver dispatches no input of its own behind the drive. Two beats use it: the cold open's first motion (60/40 → 52/48, the epic's *"a splitter drag is the first motion"*, replacing the programmatic `resizeSplit` op) and the new `film-resize` scene after the rails (52/48 → 42/58: the busy twelve-tab group gets the room the grid can spare). The document tier runs no cues, so the screenplay's readouts pin the split's order and the witness pins each drive's committed proportion from its receipt.

Two findings on the way. The first replay refused the drive as `MOUSE_SENSOR_BUSY` after the rail beat's tab click: the sensors kept their pressed element after a click that never became a drag — #19178 → PR #19180, landed on dev at `df68d34493`; this branch carries it through merge and the PR diff is the seven film files. The second was mine: the boot's first drive reported the START vector as committed, four replays of four, and a direct probe (four fresh boots, `app.driveDrag` at 0 / 1 / 2.5 / 5 s after connect) showed the engine committing 52/48 every time — the executor had read `workspace.dockModel` before the twenty-pane workspace's first view-sync adopted the reducer's document. Reading the terminal's document and waiting for adoption fixed it; the defect-note I had filed against the engine is recovered.

Evidence: L3 achieved (both drives at e7f95d9043 under the fail-closed proof: the cold open's drive 3/3 headless and 3/3 headed, beat 6's drive 3/3 headed — the headed replays on the film-stage display through the shared `NEO_FILM_DISPLAY_BOUNDS` contract; the headless replay stops at the `native-return` beat since #19181, which refuses its frame move in headless Chromium, so beat 6 is headed-only) → L3 required (AC-3, AC-5). Residual: none on the close target; the take itself stays #15252's.

## Deltas from ticket
- The committed vector is read from the splitter's terminal (`result.document`), and the beat waits for the workspace to adopt it by value: a `dockModel` read right after the terminal can still see the old vector (the boot-time race above). `synced` joins the proof.
- The proportion moved out of the screenplay's `topology-assert`s: the document tier runs the screenplay without cues (the unit spec pins the shipped `[0.6, 0.4]` after that run), so the readouts pin the split's children order and the witness reads each drive's `sizesAfter`. The ticket's "signature readout with an epsilon" became "the witness pins the proportion".
- The preview proof is an observed, bracketed sample (document → pane box → document, no terminal landed, the box moved at least `min(8, |travel|/4)` px), sampled through the cursor walk and polled until the drive settles — not a snapshot paired with a post-release box.
- `sensorDelayMs` (default 100, the Mouse sensor's own delay) lets the film cursor start with the drive's first move; the receipt records the sensor's actual thresholds so a mismatch is visible.
- The film's headless replay gate as first written (three green full replays at the head) is unreachable for any head since #19181: beat 6 is proven headed on the film-stage display; the ticket's AC-5 names the two-tier witness.
